chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Everyone who is to be judged/accounted for, is to be tormented.
Then a sayer said to him: O Messenger of Allah, then where is the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "then he will be judged an easy judgement"?
He said: That refers to the display (of deeds), meaning the turning over (of the pages).

key_terms.تَصَفُّح: The act of turning pages or a cursory glance, implying a brief and easy review.
key_terms.عَرْض: The display or presentation of deeds before God.
key_terms.مُحَاسَب: One who is subjected to detailed accounting and reckoning of deeds.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the 'easy judgement' and the 'tormented judgement' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to resolve the apparent tension between the universal accountability of all souls and the specific promise of ease for the righteous. The Imam distinguishes between 'hisaab' (a detailed, punitive accounting that brings torment) and 'hisab yasir' (a brief, non-punitive display of deeds), a distinction central to Shia eschatology regarding the varying degrees of divine justice. This clarification underscores that while all are subject to judgment, the nature of that judgment differs fundamentally based on one's spiritual state.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu’l-Jaroud, from Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, that he said:
The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Everyone who is to be judged, is to be tormented.
Then a sayer said to him: O Messenger of Allah, then where is the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «then he will be judged an easy judgement» [84:8]?
He said: That refers to turning away (from questioning). [1] It means pardoning.
